title: Settings calls the wallet ready while its only rule set is refused
body:
## Summary
The Settings layer counts a rule set the wallet now refuses (MandateListEntry.refusal) as in force, so it says "Your wallet is ready" while Rules says the set is not in force and every agent request is refused.

## Description
Three client definitions of "rules in force" disagree. lib/firstRun.ts:96 rulesInForce = window && !refusal (Charter line II, getting started); apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/setup/limits.ts:44 rulesAnswer = window && owner_sig && !refusal (Rules layer); apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/setup/circuit.ts:83 mandatesInForce = window only, fed by apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/areas/settings/SettingsLayer.tsx:55 which maps mandate_list to {id, version, notBefore, expires} and drops `refusal`. Fixed: MandateLite carries `refused`, mandatesInForce excludes it, SettingsLayer passes `!!m.refusal`; one shared predicate for the three sites.

## Flow
- a signed rule set no longer validates (NO_LONGER_FITS); mandate_list returns it with `refusal`
- Rules layer: "1 rule set is not in force" (need); Charter rules line: not done
- Settings layer: deriveCircuit counts it -> no mandate break -> settingsAnswer "Your wallet is ready" (done)
- fix: add refused to MandateLite, filter in mandatesInForce, map it in SettingsLayer; test pins settingsAnswer tone need

## Expected impact
The owner stops seeing a green "ready" while agents are refused everything; Settings agrees with Rules and the Charter. Could break: SettingsLayer tests that build mandates without refusal (unaffected, field optional).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - Settings, Rules and Charter agree on whether rules are in force
Before: 1 of 3 in-force predicates ignores refusal; a refused-only list gives settingsAnswer tone done (walked on circuit.ts:83 + SettingsLayer.tsx:55)
After: predicted 3 of 3 agree; settingsAnswer tone need, breaks [mandate]
Method: simulation - the fix needs console/areas/settings/SettingsLayer.tsx, a context this round does not own; a circuit.test case with a refused mandate is the instrument
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/setup/circuit.ts:83 `return list.filter((m) => m.notBefore <= now && now < m.expires);`
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/areas/settings/SettingsLayer.tsx:55 `mandates.data.map((m) => ({ id: m.payload.id, version: m.payload.version, notBefore: m.payload.not_before, expires: m.payload.expires }))`
apps/desktop/client/src/lib/firstRun.ts:98 `... && !m.refusal`
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/setup/limits.ts:44 `... && m.owner_sig.length > 0 && !m.refusal`
instrument: circuit.test.ts: deriveCircuit with mandates [{...M1, refused: true}] -> breaks map key includes mandate and settingsAnswer tone need (red on base); plus SettingsLayer mapping test

title: Feature docs point at four setup and safety files that no longer exist
body:
## Summary
docs/features name setup/PairingDesk.tsx, setup/CircuitView.tsx, setup/Mandates.tsx and safety/SafetySheet.tsx as where pairing, the engine picker, rule cards and the safety record live; all four were removed by the console rebuild.

## Description
Nine references across five feature docs: docs/features/pairing-relay-house.md:15,173,229; docs/features/counter-shop.md:39,124; docs/features/agents-and-engines.md:15,136; docs/features/mandates-and-rules.md:134 (also names `highlights` and `setsLine`, both gone); docs/features/book.md:157 (SafetySheet). The live homes are console/areas/connections/PairingDesk.tsx, console/areas/connections/ConnectionsLayer.tsx (EngineView), console/areas/rules/RulesLayer.tsx and console/areas/safety/SafetyLayer.tsx. context-map.json entry_points for this context name the same three dead files (director-owned).

## Flow
- reader follows docs/features/pairing-relay-house.md:173 to windows/main/setup/PairingDesk.tsx
- file does not exist
- fix: repoint each row to its console/areas home and drop removed symbols

## Expected impact
Agents and people reading the feature docs land on real files. Could break nothing (docs only).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every client path named in docs/features resolves
Before: 9 references to 4 missing files (ls on each: No such file or directory)
After: predicted 0
Method: probe - ls on the 4 paths and grep over docs/features; the edit is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
ls: cannot access apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/setup/PairingDesk.tsx / setup/Mandates.tsx / safety/SafetySheet.tsx: No such file or directory
grep "setup/PairingDesk|SafetySheet|setup/Mandates|CircuitView" docs/features -> 9 lines in 5 files
instrument: script: every backticked apps/desktop/client path in docs/features/*.md resolves on disk (9 misses on base -> 0)

title: No words guard covers the Charter's first-run copy
body:
## Summary
The WP3c words guard checks connections, deal, rewind, rules, safety and settings words, but the Charter's strings (SETUP_*, CHARTER_*, START_STEP in lib/words.ts; lib/words/setup.ts is empty) are in no guard, so a vendor name or internal word on the first-run path would pass.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/areas/settings/words.test.ts:26 AREAS = { connections, deal, rewind, rules, safety, settings }. apps/desktop/client/src/lib/words/setup.ts holds `export {}`; the Charter imports CHARTER_TITLE, CHARTER_STATE, SETUP_STEP_COPY, SETUP_WAITING, SETUP_NOT_DONE, START_STEP, SAFETY_PROMISE etc. from lib/words.ts. UX-GUIDE checklist: "the area's words guard passes". Fixed: the guard also walks the Charter's exports (or they move to lib/words/setup.ts, which the guard then lists).

## Flow
- someone adds "Claude" or "mandate_sign" to SETUP_STEP_COPY
- no test fails
- fix: add the Charter exports to the guard's AREAS and seed a vendor word to see it go red

## Expected impact
The first screen a new merchant sees gets the same vendor/internal-word protection as every other area. Could break: an existing Charter string that already violates (that is a finding, not a breakage).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - first-run copy is guarded like the other areas
Before: 0 of the Charter's word exports are under the words guard
After: predicted all of them, with a seeded vendor word going red
Method: simulation - the guard file lives in the settings area this round does not own
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/areas/settings/words.test.ts:26 `const AREAS = { connections, deal, rewind, rules, safety, settings };`
apps/desktop/client/src/lib/words/setup.ts:7 `export {};`
instrument: words.test.ts extended with the Charter exports; seed "claude-code app" into a copy of SETUP_STEP_COPY in the test and watch VENDOR go red

title: Swap the pairing words' raw 30px for --fs-display
body:
## Summary
connections.css sizes the four pairing words at a raw 30px under a header that says tokens only.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/areas/connections.css:108 font-size: 30px; --fs-display is 30px in the main window (design/tokens.css:93) and only differs in the Tumbler, which never renders the desk. The code at :92 uses a raw 40px with no matching token.

## Flow
- render the desk in the main window
- computed font-size 30px either way

## Expected impact
None measurable.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - words follow the type scale
Before: 30px computed in the main window
After: 30px computed in the main window
Method: probe - token values compared for the only window that renders the desk
Result: not-better
Gate: none
